correctness.rationale: Multiplying y′=-x−βx⁵+αx³y² by e^{−αx⁴/2}y and using V′=e^{−αx⁴/2}(x+βx⁵) exactly conserves H=½e^{−αx⁴/2}y²+V(x). The potential is even, strictly monotone on x>0, with Gaussian ceiling E*=√π/(2√(2α))(1+β/α). For 0<E<E* energy level is a compact periodic oval, E=E* two monotone complete branches with critical speed²~(1+βx⁴)/(αx²), and E>E* two finite-time escaping branches. The one-sided Laplace estimate for R(x)=E*−V(x) yields critical x(t) growth and supercritical tail e^{−αx⁴/4}/(αx³√(2(E−E*))). For periods the ratio of periodic to critical speed away from x=A is 1−R(A)/R(x); a strip h_A=K log A/A³ has reciprocal-speed integral o(1), controlling the singular turning point. Integrating critical reciprocal speed yields T~2√α A² (β=0), T~4√(α/β)log A (β>0); substituting log(E*/δ)~αA⁴/2 gives the stated sqrt-log and log-log laws. Time-preserving coordinate z=∫e^{−αx⁴/4}dx yields local g(z)=z+(β−α/5)z⁵+..., period correction (α−5β)A⁴/16. Independently checked the conservation identity and local coefficient symbolically; finite quadrature cannot establish limits.
